stem: A fintech company's platform team already standardizes on Kubernetes APIs and manifests and wants a managed Kubernetes control plane so its workloads stay portable across clouds.

choices.text: Amazon ECS with the EC2 launch type
Amazon EKS running the team's existing Kubernetes manifests
A self-managed Kubernetes control plane the team installs and patches on its own EC2 instances
Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type

rationale: Amazon EKS runs a managed Kubernetes control plane, which fits a team that already standardizes on Kubernetes APIs, manifests, and the broader Kubernetes ecosystem, including portability to other clouds. Amazon ECS is AWS's own container orchestrator with an AWS-native scheduler; it does not expose the Kubernetes API the team has already standardized on, no matter how its compute is provisioned. A self-managed Kubernetes control plane on EC2 the team installs and patches itself is the opposite of a managed control plane, putting the operational burden the team wants to avoid back on them. Fargate for ECS removes the EC2 layer for ECS tasks specifically, but ECS tasks still are not the Kubernetes API and manifests the team's tooling depends on.
